---
title: "Rebuild the GenoDisc secondary GWAS (LDSC rG) reference panel"
author: "GenoDisc"
output: html_document
---

## Why this exists

The reference panel for GenoDisc's LDSC genetic-correlation analysis lives at
`pipeline_resources/data/secondary_gwas/<code>.sumstats.gz` (plus a
`sumstat_repo.csv` catalog). Historically these files were prepared by
different people at different times with different tools, so the panel was a
mix of files munged against different SNP sets. When the user's cleaned GWAS
was paired with a mis-munged reference,
`ldsc.py --rg` threw:

```
KeyError: 'Incompatible alleles in .sumstats files. ...
    Did you forget to use --merge-alleles?'
```

LDSC's wrapper exits **0** on this error and `process_ldsc_gencor.R` catches
the `ERROR computing rg` marker and returns an `NA` row — the failure was
silent. At least one panel file (`CHOL35.sumstats.gz`) was outright corrupt
(header + `nrow(w_hm3)` empty rows).

The fix: re-munge every reference GWAS through **the same script the pipeline
uses for the primary GWAS** — `GenoUtils::sumstat_cleaner.R --merge_alleles
w_hm3.snplist`. Reference and query then share IUPAC coding, allele
harmonisation, and HapMap3 restriction, and `--rg` can pair any two without
allele-set surprises.

## Scope of this rebuild

- Rebuild only the codes that are currently shipping as `.sumstats.gz`.
- Strict EUR ancestry (parentheticals stripped, then exact `eur|european`).
- Do **not** modify anything under `/scratch/prj/gwas_sumstats/cleaned/` —
  that is the shared read-only source. Everything is read from there and
  written to the panel dir / this misc dir.
- Do not touch the pipeline rules or the web-app-generated
  `gencor_gwas_list.txt`.

## Layout

Files in this directory:

| File                       | Purpose                                                  |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rebuild_secondary_gwas.Rmd` | This document.                                         |
| `activate_pipe_env.sh`     | Activates the pipeline conda env for standalone scripts. |
| `build_targets.R`          | Builds `targets.csv` from the current panel + repo CSV.  |
| `munge_one.sh`             | Munges one code through `sumstat_cleaner.R`; stages it.  |
| `submit_munge.sh`          | SLURM array wrapper around `munge_one.sh`.               |
| `validate_and_publish.R`   | Validates staging, publishes, rebuilds `sumstat_repo.csv`. |
| `targets.csv`              | Generated: driver table (code, source, N, metadata).     |
| `targets_excluded.csv`     | Generated: codes dropped pre-munge (non-EUR / no source).|
| `rebuild_log.csv`          | Generated: final status per input code.                  |
| `logs/`                    | Generated: per-code worker logs + SLURM stdout/stderr.   |

Staging (intermediate `.cleaned.*` files, ~10 GB) is written **outside**
this repo dir, under the panel dir itself:

| Path                                                | Purpose                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<SGWAS>/staging/<code>.sumstats.gz`                | Staged munged file before it's promoted to `<SGWAS>/<code>.sumstats.gz`. |
| `<SGWAS>/staging/work/<code>/`                      | Per-code `.cleaned.*` outputs from `sumstat_cleaner.R`.     |

where `<SGWAS>` =
`/scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/pipeline_resources/data/secondary_gwas`.
Once you're satisfied with a rebuild, wipe it with
`rm -rf <SGWAS>/staging`.

## Prerequisites

The GenoDisc snakemake pipeline must have been run at least once so its
conda env (`envs/main.yaml`, containing GenoUtils + data.table) has been
built under `/scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/conda-envs/`.
`activate_pipe_env.sh` picks the most-recently-modified matching env.

## Step 1 — build the driver table

```{bash build-targets, eval=FALSE}
cd /scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/repo/current/pipeline/misc/secondary_gwas
source ./activate_pipe_env.sh
Rscript --vanilla ./build_targets.R
# -> targets.csv (rows to munge)
# -> targets_excluded.csv (codes dropped for ancestry / no source)
```

`targets.csv` columns:
`code, source_path, n, ancestry, phenotype_type, category, trait_label,
short_label, n_cases, n_controls, sample_size_discovery, pmid`.

## Step 2 — submit the munge array to SLURM

`munge_one.sh` is a standalone worker (`./munge_one.sh <code>`); `submit_munge.sh`
wraps it as a SLURM array job (one array task per row of `targets.csv`).

**Submit from a login node** — KCL ERC-HPC compute nodes don't have `sbatch`.

```{bash submit-slurm, eval=FALSE}
cd /scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/repo/current/pipeline/misc/secondary_gwas
N=$(($(wc -l < targets.csv) - 1))
sbatch --array=1-${N}%10 submit_munge.sh
# %10 caps concurrent tasks; drop/raise to taste.
# Progress:
#   squeue -u $USER -n gd-munge-secondary
#   tail -f logs/munge-<JOBID>_*.out
```

Per-task resources default to `--mem=8G --time=1:00:00 --cpus-per-task=1`
(see the `#SBATCH` header of `submit_munge.sh`). The heaviest sumstats
(a few hundred MB gzipped) fit well inside 8G; runtime is 2–10 min each.

### Alternative: local xargs on a big compute node

If you're already sitting on a fat compute node (KCL `erc-hpc-comp*` nodes
have ~5 CPUs / 1 TB RAM) and don't want the SLURM round-trip, the same
worker runs directly:

```{bash local-parallel, eval=FALSE}
cd /scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/repo/current/pipeline/misc/secondary_gwas
awk -F',' 'NR>1 {print $1}' targets.csv | \
  xargs -P 5 -I{} bash -c \
    './munge_one.sh "$1" > logs/munge-"$1".out 2>&1 && \
     echo "OK $1" || echo "FAIL $1 exit=$?"' _ {} \
    | tee logs/run_all.log
```

Both paths write the exact same artifacts
(`<SGWAS>/staging/<code>.sumstats.gz` +
`<SGWAS>/staging/work/<code>/*` + `<MISC>/logs/munge-<code>.out`), so
downstream steps don't care which was used.

## Step 3 — validate + publish

```{bash validate-publish, eval=FALSE}
cd /scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/repo/current/pipeline/misc/secondary_gwas
source ./activate_pipe_env.sh
Rscript --vanilla ./validate_and_publish.R
```

`validate_and_publish.R`:

1. Reads each `<SGWAS>/staging/<code>.sumstats.gz` and checks:
   - header = `CHR SNP BP A1 A2 Z N` (the same schema `sumstat_qc.smk`
     writes for the primary GWAS at
     `{gwas}.cleaned.munged.mergealleles.sumstats.gz`),
   - row count ≥ 500,000,
   - every SNP is in `w_hm3.snplist`.
   Any failure produces a `munge_failed` / `low_snp_count` / `not_hm3` row.
2. Writes `rebuild_log.csv` (one row per input code: shipped, excluded,
   failed).
3. Backs up the existing `sumstat_repo.csv` to
   `sumstat_repo.csv.bak-preRebuild-<YYYYMMDD>` (unless a backup for today
   already exists).
4. Copies passing files into
   `pipeline_resources/data/secondary_gwas/<code>.sumstats.gz`; removes any
   previously-shipped `.gz` for a code that no longer ships (so downstream
   jobs can't pick up stale data).
5. Rebuilds `sumstat_repo.csv` with a slim schema (`code, trait_category,
   trait_label, short_label, ancestry, phenotype_type, n_cases, n_controls,
   sample_size_discovery, pmid`) — only rows for currently-shipped codes.
   `short_label` uses the curated value when non-empty and ≤ 40 chars, else
   auto-shortens `trait_label` by stripping parentheticals and trailing
   `: <suffix>` clauses.

## Consumer contracts (unchanged)

- **Pipeline** (`sumstat_qc.smk` `ldsc_gencor`) reads a space-separated
  `gencor_gwas_list.txt` (written by the web app) with columns
  `name path population n sampling prevalence mean sd label [extras…]`.
- **Web app** reads `sumstat_repo.csv` (columns
  `code, trait_category, trait_label, short_label, …`) to build the picker
  and write `gencor_gwas_list.txt`.
- **Panel file format**: `CHR SNP BP A1 A2 Z N` (tab-separated, gzipped).
  LDSC uses only `SNP A1 A2 Z N` and ignores the extras.

## Verifying the rebuild

```{bash verify, eval=FALSE}
cd /scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/pipeline_resources/data/secondary_gwas

# 1. Every shipped file has the pipeline mergealleles header.
for f in *.sumstats.gz; do zcat "$f" | head -1; done | sort -u
# Expect exactly one line: CHR<TAB>SNP<TAB>BP<TAB>A1<TAB>A2<TAB>Z<TAB>N

# 2. Every shipped file has a metadata row and vice-versa.
comm -3 \
  <(ls *.sumstats.gz | sed 's/\.sumstats\.gz$//' | sort) \
  <(awk -F',' 'NR>1 {print $1}' sumstat_repo.csv | sort)
# Expect no output.

# 3. Ad-hoc rG on the pipeline's known-good test primary.
source /scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/bin/activate_genodisc.sh
LDSC=/scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/pipeline_resources/software/ldsc
PRIM=/scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/repo/current/pipeline/tests/output/results/COAD01chr22/gwas_sumstat/COAD01chr22.cleaned.munged.mergealleles.sumstats.gz
LD=/scratch/prj/neurohackpain/GenoDisc/pipeline_resources/data/ldsc/eur_w_ld_chr/
for ref in BODY11 ADHD06 SCHI04; do
  python2.7 "$LDSC/ldsc.py" --rg "$PRIM","$PWD/${ref}.sumstats.gz" \
      --ref-ld-chr "$LD" --w-ld-chr "$LD" --out /tmp/rg_${ref}
  grep -A1 "^p1 " /tmp/rg_${ref}.log
done
# Expect no "Incompatible alleles" errors and non-NA rg values.
```

## Adding a new GWAS later

1. Add the new code + metadata to `sumstat_repo.csv` (via the web app or by
   hand editing the backup + re-slimming through `validate_and_publish.R`).
2. Make sure `<CODE>.gz` exists under `/scratch/prj/gwas_sumstats/cleaned/`.
3. Re-run steps 1–3 above. `build_targets.R` picks up the new code
   automatically because it iterates the current panel dir ∪ repo rows.
